handoff: review#1 approve: AC1-AC6 met and tested (status.test.ts, moved inbox tests), AC7 checked by hand in implement; full suite 1249 pass, typecheck green. No blocking findings. Minor: the notice is skipped under --json/--segment (a reasonable reading of B13, but unstated in the spec). Nit: --ttl without --segment is silently ignored. Printed norn inbox / norn status <key> strings are deferred to slice 14 as planned.

findings.title: The notice is skipped under --json instead of being shown
findings.detail:
B13 says only that 'stdout and `--json` output are unaffected'. The code does not show or spend the notice under `--json` (or `--segment`). This is a reasonable reading (a script should not spend the notice a person needs) and the handoff records it as a decision, but the spec does not state it.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep the behaviour. Record it in the spec's Plan or decisions (slice 15 PRD amendment) so it is stated, not just implied.

findings.title: --ttl and the inbox flags are accepted in the wrong mode
findings.detail:
`norn status --ttl 5s` (without --segment) and `norn status --segment --details` parse fine and the extra flag is silently ignored. `--since` without `--history` is refused, so the command already uses that pattern elsewhere. Also, `help status --json` lists `segment` and `ttl` among status's options while its usage line hides them.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Refuse `--ttl` without `--segment` (usageError, as for `--since`), or accept the silent ignore on purpose.
